articles.summary: Kimberly Hefner, who was married to Hugh Hefner from 1989 until their divorce was finalized in 2010, has taken to social media to share a statement in support of her late husband after his former wife, Crystal Harris, alleged she experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse while…
body: She continued: “Losing Hef was devastating, and his absence is still deeply felt. I had the privilege of knowing and loving the man behind the public image, and I will always treasure the life and memories we shared. I will always believe the world was a better place because he was in it. I am forever grateful and blessed.”

Before they tied the knot, Kimberly and Hugh met when she was modeling for Playboy’s Playmate of the Month centerfold. Hugh met Harris at a Halloween party at the Playboy Mansion when she was a 21-year-old college student. She moved into the mansion shortly thereafter and married Hugh in 2012. The two remained together until his death in Sept. 2017, after which Harris published her 2024 memoir “Only Say Good Things: Surviving Playboy and Finding Myself,” in which she revealed her experiences at the mansion.

articles.title: Quentin Tarantino Play ‘The Popinjay Cavalier,’ Starring Sacha Baron Cohen, to Open on West End in March
articles.summary: Quentin Tarantino’s first-ever stage play, “The Popinjay Cavalier” starring Sacha Baron Cohen, will open at London’s Phoenix Theatre in March. Written and directed by Tarantino, the play — described as a “swashbuckling comedy” — will hold previews from Feb. 23, with opening night set for March 18.
body: Quentin Tarantino ‘s first-ever stage play, “The Popinjay Cavalier” starring Sacha Baron Cohen, will open at London’s Phoenix Theatre in March.

Set in 1830s Europe, “The Popinjay Cavalier” is a “rambunctious comedy of deception and disguise inspired by the grand swashbuckling epics of stage and screen,” as the play’s synopsis reads. “A sweeping celebration of theatre and its heightened romance, told with Tarantino’s signature style and unmistakable wit, ‘The Popinjay Cavalier’ is inspired by the classic swashbuckler genre of old Hollywood, including the writings of George Bruce, Ernst Vajda and Jesse Lasky Jr.”

Added Baron Cohen, whose casting was first revealed last month: “Quentin called, I said yes before he even got to say his first ‘motherf—er’. When the best director in the world calls, you don’t ask questions. I am beyond delighted that we will be losing our West End virginity together, I have made him promise not to be gentle.”

Producers Tom Rothman, chairman and CEO of Sony Pictures Entertainment’s Motion Picture group, and Sonia Friedman said it is a “joy and an honor to be developing this play with Quentin — and absolutely quite an adventure.”

articles.title: After Kelly Clarkson Slams Brooklyn Novelty Store, Shop Says the ‘One-of-a-Kind’ Singing Bird She Wanted Wasn’t Actually For Sale
articles.summary: After Kelly Clarkson took to X on Saturday to share her experience “being treated like Julia Roberts” in “Pretty Woman” during a visit to Art of Play, a novelty shop in Brooklyn, the local business is responding to her claims, saying it has received “widespread outrage” since and explaining that…
body: On Sunday, the business posted a multi-slide carousel to the store’s Instagram account sharing their side of the story. They began by clarifying that the item Clarkson inquired about purchasing was “a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton who plays an important role in the magic shows we host here.” “Molly is permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale. However, the negative experience Kelly described on Twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop,” the caption read.

The business continued to note that “whether someone comes in to make a purchase or simply look around for a while, they are equally welcome. We greet everyone who walks in the door with the invitation to ‘pick things up and play.’ And they do, many stay for hours enjoying our puzzles, games and toys.”
Art of Play also acknowledged the significant backlash they’ve been receiving since Clarkson’s statement, before quoting the singer and concluding the message.
In a Feb. 2025 Instagram post’s caption, the business wrote that Molly is the store’s “beloved shop bird” and “mascot,” and she is one of the few items in Art of Play that has a “Do Not Touch” sign.

articles.title: John Stamos Addresses Mike Love’s Health as Beach Boys Concert Footage Raises Concerns: ‘We Don’t Know What the Future Holds — We Have Tonight’
articles.summary: Following many Beach Boys fans and followers expressing concern for Mike Love after seeing footage from the group’s Saturday night show in Cincinnati, John Stamos has stepped in with a statement acknowledging that Love is in poor health as they are doing these shows and suggesting that his longtime…
body: The Beach Boys had been off the road since July, canceling several months of dates as Love addressed health concerns, with a pledge to take up where they left off. More gigs kept being canceled, one by one, until the group finally resumed action, first with a private performance and then a return to public touring with Saturday’s Cincinnati show. But many were alarmed by what they saw in fan-posted video, with Love appearing much weaker and less engaged than he was even in July’s shows.

The frontman for the group for the last six and a half decades remained seated and largely motionless for the entire show in Ohio, not taking any of the many lead vocals he was still doing when the Beach Boys performed for three nights at the Hollywood Bowl in July. One short clip that quickly circulated on social media showed Stamos urging Love to do some hand gestures from his seat, and the Beach Boys’ mainstay gamely complying, but without much apparent energy, before going back to sitting in place.

articles.title: Wildwood review – Laika’s pleasingly old fashioned stop-motion magic-forest odyssey
articles.summary: The makers of Coraline return with their distinctive animation style in a magical tale of a secret world of strange beasts, talking animals and evil governesses. Here is an engaging family movie from the Portland-based Laika studio that created Coraline.
body: They are stunned when a bunch (or rather a murder) of crows gather with Hitchcockian menace in a kids’ play area, swoop down and carry poor little Mac off to their forest domain. Plucky (and also terrified) Prue and Curtis give chase and enter the dark and trackless forest, and find it is a parallel world, undreamt of by the ordinary human world, populated by all manner of loquacious beasts and oppressed humans. Their rule is divided between the supercilious and incompetent governor (Marc Evan Jackson) and the evil dowager governess, voiced with relish by Carey Mulligan, who has at her command a redcoat army of coyotes.

The dowager governess has a wrenching sadness in her heart, due to an awful loss and a tragic attempt at a cover-up, which the film shows us in the opening section. Prue and Curtis, though separated by the action, are to come together for their big showdown with this wicked witch of the forest and a reckoning also with the Wildwood’s bandit leader and freedom fighter Brendan, voiced by Mahershala Ali.

articles.title: Another Marvel Director Nearly Made The Young Sheldon Pilot
articles.summary: The Young Sheldon pilot was helmed by Iron Man director Jon Favreau, but if he hadn't been available another Marvel director was next on the list.
body: Jon Favreau is about as accomplished as one can be in the realm of directing successful projects. No only did he help kickstart the Marvel Cinematic Universe with "Iron Man," but he's also behind several hugely successful TV shows as well. The first one that comes to mind is "The Mandalorian" in the "Star Wars" galaxy, but he also directed the pilot for "The Big Bang Theory" spin-off "Young Sheldon." If he hadn't, though, another Marvel director very well could have.

In an interview with Entertainment Weekly, series co-creator Steve Molaro explained that Favreau was the first choice, as Chuck Lorre was a fan. "I had a friendship with Jon Favreau, so when we were floating around who would be a great fit, I told Chuck I kind of know him," Molaro said. He further explained that it was 2016's "The Jungle Book" that really got things going.
At the time, Favreau was also working on 2019's "The Lion King" remake, but he still managed to carve out some time to direct the "Young Sheldon" pilot.

articles.title: Paramount Is Both The Best And Worst Thing To Happen To Avatar: The Last Airbender
articles.summary: Paramount has repeatedly fumbled the Avatar: The Last Airbender franchise, but announcements at New York Comic-Con 2026 offer hope of a turnaround.
body: With its spectacular combination of epic fantasy, nuanced storytelling, compelling characters, mature themes, and stunning martial arts action, "Avatar: The Last Airbender" is one of the greatest shows of the 21st century.

It's been over 20 years since "The Last Airbender" premiered, and since then we've had dozens of books and comics, two live-action remakes, two sequel series, and one sequel movie. In theory, a great time to be an "Avatar" fan, right? In 2026 alone we've had the very first feature film animation in the franchise, with the return of Aang and his friends as young adults in a brand new adventure. And most recently we got "Avatar: Seven Havens," the first new series in over a decade, with the next avatar in the cycle – actually, two Avatars.
points: Paramount has repeatedly fumbled the Avatar: The Last Airbender franchise, but announcements at New York Comic-Con 2026 offer hope of a turnaround.

articles.title: Non-Alcoholic Drink Pairings Up Their Game (and their Prices) at L.A.’s Top Restaurants
articles.summary: Alcohol consumption has plummeted so drastically in L.A. that establishments are offering elevated zero-proof accompaniments to make their margins.
body: Kim Stodel, bar director at three-Michelin-starred Providence a few blocks west of the Paramount lot in Hollywood, steeps charred sweet corn in jasmine green tea on a recent afternoon. “I have a suspicion that adding this burnt aroma will accentuate things, taking it over the edge in the way I’m hoping,” he explains of tweaking this accompaniment to an abalone dish on the seafood restaurant’s tasting menu. It’s part of Stodel’s extensive prep and constant experimentation for his nonalcoholic pairings program.

Providence has been around for two decades, Stodel overseeing drinks for more than half that span. But he’s only been concocting elaborate spirit-free progressions in the past two years. “The NA category is exploding,” Stodel says, “and we’re all still beginners, exploring.” Related Stories. articles.title: William Shatner's '70s Sci-Fi TV Movie Featured A Guest-Star From A Notorious Star Trek Episode
articles.summary: William Shatner and Kim Darby both appeared in the 1972 TV movie The People, but they also acted together in a controversial Star Trek episode.
body: In 1972, Francis Ford Coppola served as the executive producer for John Korty's TV movie "The People," based largely on the story "Pottage" by celebrated sci-fi author Zenna Henderson. "The People" stars Kim Darby as a schoolteacher named Malodye, who travels out to a very, very remote community to teach the local children. The community is very Amish-like in their customs and very eerie. The children, for instance, are forbidden from doing any of the fun things that Melodye suggests during class. Indeed, the very concept of "fun" seems to be banned.

The sci-fi twist is that all the members of this community are actually extraterrestrials who emigrated to Earth when they lost their home planet to environmental disasters. The aliens have been on Earth since the late 19th century, but have long been attacked and pilloried for their mild alien superpowers. The overall film is super-mellow, with William Shatner playing a character named Dr. Curtis. Coppola's father, Carmine, wrote the score. The movie is pastoral and calm and doesn't really seem to feature much in the way of actual drama.
points: William Shatner and Kim Darby both appeared in the 1972 TV movie The People, but they also acted together in a controversial Star Trek episode.

articles.title: Robert De Niro's First Major Movie Was A Controversial Comedy From A Legendary Director
articles.summary: A very young Robert De Niro starred in this Brian De Palma-directed comedy film, which was fairly controversial at the time due to its content.
body: Brian De Palma's 1968 comedy movie "Greetings," starring a young Robert De Niro, was the very first narrative film to receive an "X" rating. Keep in mind, though, this was before the adult film industry began unofficially co-opting the rating and the term "X-rated" referred exclusively to porn.

It's likely you haven't seen "Greetings," as it is something of an obscurity. It was only the second feature that De Palma directed after the wild experimental film "Murder a la Mod," released earlier in the same year. "Greetings" also marked the first time De Niro and De Palma worked together, followed by "The Wedding Party" (1969), "Hi, Mom!" (1970), and "The Untouchables" (1987). Of course, by 1987, the pair had become gigantic celebrities, with De Niro being considered one of the best actors to ever to do.

"Greetings" is currently available to stream on Prime Video, and fans of experimental 1960s art films will certainly want to take a look. Free-form, narrative-less, and controversial movies are kind of my jam.

articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen and 300 Ali G Look-Alikes Descend on London Ahead of New Movie ‘Who Iz I?’
articles.summary: Amazon MGM Studios is set to release the star's comedy 'Ali G: Who Iz I?' in theaters for one week on Oct. 23.
body: Sacha Baron Cohen and 300 fans, all of whom were dressed like the performer’s satirical character Ali G, took to the streets of London on Sunday ahead of the release of Ali G: Who Iz I?

Cohen was decked out in a yellow “Ali G” hoodie and matching pants as the hip-hop journalist that he originated on the sketch comedy series Da Ali G Show, which debuted in the U.K. in 2000 and later aired on HBO. Accompanied by the hundreds of individuals dressed similarly, some of whom were sporting wrap-around sunglasses and even fake goatees, the star led his cohorts on a tour of London landmarks that culminated in Cohen overseeing the Ali G Lookalike Competition.
